answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line sits at 94% with no buffer, so delivery continuity dominates. Renewing is the only action that historically kept integration and scheduled deliveries intact (c1). Defer is not safe here: unlike the non-critical month-to-month case (c5), lapse would halt supply. Incumbent has already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms would likely burn the single decision without securing the 18% cut. Switch is the inherited cost lever (c2) but would raise delivery risk under current tightness; verifying c2 before locking that out. Cost-mandate miss and single-source exposure on a no-buffer line are flagged; last-year onboarding speed may not transfer.
